title: Federal Rule 12 — defenses and motions
summary: Rule 12 provides distinct ways to respond to a complaint, including objections to authority, legal sufficiency, excessive vagueness, and specified material within the pleading. Each motion has its own purpose and preservation rules.

sections.Role in the course: Rule 12 provides distinct ways to respond to a complaint, including objections to authority, legal sufficiency, excessive vagueness, and specified material within the pleading. Each motion has its own purpose and preservation rules.
sections.What to examine: Identify whether the objection concerns jurisdiction, service, venue, failure to state a claim, a required party, inability to frame a response, or matter to be struck. Garcia illustrates why a court may preserve a claim while requiring detail and removing particular allegations.
